title: Security & Compliance: RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency, SDLC, Incident Response, Evidence Workflows, and Risk Exceptions
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview:

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's security and compliance controls for role-based access control (RBAC) and authentication, audit logging, data residency and retention, secure software development lifecycle (SDLC), incident response for security events, compliance evidence collection workflows, and the process for requesting and approving risk exceptions. It is intended for engineering managers, platform and infra engineers, SRE, product security, and compliance stakeholders.

Scope and Applicability:
- Applies to all Redwood-managed control plane and customer-facing control plane components (hosted API, Dedicated control plane, and Private control plane where Redwood provides managed services).
- Covers human access, machine/service accounts, CI/CD, telemetry pipelines, storage systems, backups, and audit/evidence artifacts.
- Does not replace customer-specific contractual controls; see customer-specific compliance attachments where applicable.

Owners and Contact:
- Document owner: Maya Chen (Security Engineering)
- Primary operations owner: Eng-SRE (oncall@redwood.example.com)
- Compliance contact: Priya Singh (Compliance)
- Escalation: Security Pager: +1-555-0100 (see oncall roster)

1) RBAC and Authentication

Principles:
- Least privilege by default; roles are narrowly scoped and reviewed quarterly.
- Separation of duties: no single role should approve, deploy, and audit the same change set in production environments.
- All human access must be via SSO (Okta). MFA required for all interactive access.

Role Catalog (summary):
| Role | Scope | Typical Members | Adminable By | Review Frequency |
|-----|-------|-----------------|--------------|------------------|
| platform-admin | Global infra provisioning, IAM, networking | Infra leads | Security | Quarterly |
| runtime-operator | Model serving clusters, autoscaling policies | Runtime SRE | Eng-Platform | Monthly |
| dev | Non-prod app environments, build pipelines | Engineers | Team Leads | Quarterly |
| read-only-audit | Read-only access to logs, dashboards | Auditors, Compliance | Security | Quarterly |

Provisioning and Deprovisioning Flow:
1. Access requests must be submitted via the internal access portal (https://access.redwood.internal) with business justification and expiration date.
2. Team manager approves the request; security performs entitlement review for high-risk roles (>90 days, global_admin).
3. Requests for permanent privileged roles require explicit executive sponsor and justification.
4. Automated deprovisioning: Idle accounts (no activity for 90 days) are flagged and disabled.

Service Accounts and Keys:
- Short-lived service credentials are strongly preferred. Use the Secrets Manager integrated role-based issuance (STS) for ephemeral tokens.
- Long-lived keys require documented justification, rotation every 30 days, and storage in the secrets vault.
- Ownership: each service account must list an owner and an emergency contact in the secrets metadata.

Authentication Standards:
- SSO: Okta as primary identity provider (IdP); SCIM automated provisioning for user lifecycle.
- Federated access: restrict external IdPs to approved partner accounts; require SCIM mapping and audit.
- Passwords: discouraged for interactive access; system accounts require unique seeded secrets and vault storage.

2) Audit Logging

Goals and Requirements:
- Provide immutable, tamper-evident logs for identity, access, configuration changes, and high-risk runtime events.
- Support forensic analysis and compliance evidence with at least 3 months of hot logs and longer-term cold storage.

Events to Capture (minimum):
- Authentication attempts (success/failure), token issuance and revocation
- IAM changes (role grants, role revocations, policy updates)
- Administrative actions (deploys, canary/promote, rollback)
- Access to sensitive artifacts (secrets retrieval, key downloads)
- Data export operations, backup exports, and syncs to external storage

Log Pipeline Architecture (summary):
- Ingest: Applications and infra emit structured JSON events to centralized ingesters (Fluentd/Vector).
- Transport: Events are forwarded over mTLS to the centralized logging cluster (Elasticsearch/Opensearch or managed service).
- Retention: Hot index retention: 90 days. Cold archive: S3 encrypted with KMS, lifecycle to 7 years for select artifacts.

Integrity and Monitoring:
- Logs are signed at ingestion using HMAC with a rotation-aware key.
- Integrity SLO: 99.9% of ingestion received within 1 minute of event generation.
- Alerting: Missing expected heartbeat from critical sources triggers a P1 in 5 minutes.

Access and Querying:
- Sensitive fields (PII, secrets) are redacted at source where feasible and stored with strict access controls.
- Access to raw logs requires read-only-audit role and an active justification in the access portal; access requests for specific time windows require approval by Security.

Retention and Deletion Policy:
| Artifact | Hot Retention | Archive Retention | Notes |
|---------|---------------|-------------------|-------|
| Auth logs | 90 days | 7 years (filtered) | Audit-grade; archived per customer/regional requirements |
| App debug logs | 14 days | 90 days | Short-lived; may be purged unless tagged for investigation |
| Backup manifests | 365 days | 7 years | Needed for restore and legal holds |

3) Data Residency and Retention

Region Mapping and Controls:
- Supported regions: us-west-2, us-east-1, eu-west-1, eu-central-1, ap-southeast-1 (customer opt-in).
- Data classification: Public, Internal, Sensitive, Regulated (e.g., customer PHI/PII).
- Regulated data must be stored only in customer-approved regions; see the Data Residency matrix.

Data Residency Matrix (excerpt):
| Data Type | Default Region | Allowed Regions | Retention Policy | Owner |
|-----------|----------------|-----------------|------------------|-------|
| Customer logs (non-PII) | us-west-2 | us-west-2, eu-west-1 | 90 days | Platform |
| Customer PII | region-specific per contract | Contracted region only | per-customer retention | Customer Success |
| Backups | us-west-2 (primary), s3-cross-region-archive | Customer opt-in | 365 days+legal hold | Eng-Infra |

Retention Strategy:
1. Define retention at dataset level in the metastore and enforce via lifecycle policies.
2. Apply legal hold flags for customer incidents and audits; legal hold overrides deletion.
3. Quarterly retention audit to validate lifecycle policies and S3/GCS lifecycle rules.

4) Secure SDLC (Secure Software Development Lifecycle)

Build and Pipeline Controls:
- CI Gate Requirements: All merges to release branches must pass: unit tests, integration tests, SCA (software composition analysis), static analysis (SAST), dependency license check, and provenance check.
- Secrets scanning: Block builds that contain detected secrets in code.
- Signed commits and enforced branch protections for main/release branches.

Review and Approval:
- Pull Request rules: Minimum 2 reviewers for critical production services; at least one reviewer must be from a different team when possible.
- Security code review: Every high/critical vulnerability requires a security review ticket and risk assessment before merge.

Dependency and Build Provenance:
- Reproducible builds for runtime artifacts; artifacts stored in internal artifact registry (Nexus/Artifactory) with immutability for release artifacts.
- SBOMs generated for all release images; SBOMs stored alongside artifacts for audit.

Runtime Hardening:
- Container image scanning (CVE severity >= HIGH blocks promotion).
- Runtime process-level isolation for multi-tenant hostings; mandatory seccomp and capability restrictions.

5) Incident Response: Security-specific Procedures

Detection and Triage:
1. Automated detection: IDS/EDR, anomaly detection on telemetry, and log-based rules (thresholds and behavioral analytics).
2. Triage within 15 minutes for alerts classified as potential data exfiltration or privilege misuse.

Containment and Eradication Steps (example: suspected compromised service account):
1. Rotate affected credentials immediately (STS revoke + rotate secrets).
2. Isolate affected hosts/services from network via orchestration layer (autoscaler suspend) and apply access firewall rule.
3. Snapshot affected VMs/containers for forensic investigation.
4. Review auth logs and network flow logs (see Log Query examples in Appendix).

Notification and Regulatory Requirements:
- Internal notification: Security Pager and CISO within 30 minutes for any confirmed sensitive data exposure.
- External notification: Follow legal and customer contractual timelines; legal lead to coordinate external disclosures.

Post-Incident Activities:
- Postmortem with timeline and root cause within 7 days.
- Evidence preservation: Ensure logs, snapshots, and chain-of-custody notes are stored in the evidence repository (immutable store).
- Remediation verification: Security verifies fixes and monitors for recurrence for 90 days.

6) Compliance Evidence Workflows

Control Families and Evidence Artifacts (examples):
- Access Control (AC): IAM policies, quarterly entitlement reviews, access request tickets.
- Logging & Monitoring (LM): Retention config, log integrity proofs, alerting runbooks.
- Change Management (CM): ADRs, change tickets, canary release logs, rollback records.
- SDLC (SD): SBOMs, SAST/SCA reports, signed release artifact manifests.

Evidence Collection Playbook (auditor request flow):
1. Auditor submits evidence request with scope and time window to compliance@redwood.example.com.
2. Compliance triages and issues an evidence ticket in the internal tracker.
3. Engineering owner collects artifacts and deposits them into the evidence repository (immutable S3 prefix) with metadata (owner, purpose, time window).
4. Compliance validates artifacts and timestamps the evidence in the control workbook.
5. After audit close, artifacts remain in archive per retention policy unless purged per legal.

Evidence Repository and Access:
- Evidence is stored in an encrypted, access-controlled S3 prefix with MFA-delete enabled for high-sensitivity artifacts.
- Access is logged and requires temporary elevation via the access portal; read-only audit role is default for auditors.

Audit Readiness Checklist:
- Quarterly control self-assessment completed and signed by control owners.
- SBOMs and release manifests for last 12 months available.
- IAM entitlement report for all high-privilege roles exported within 24 hours.

7) Risk Exceptions and Residual Risk Management

Exception Request Process:
1. Owner submits exception request in the access portal with technical justification, compensating controls, and a fixed expiry date (max 90 days for high-risk exceptions).
2. Security reviews and assigns risk rating (Low / Medium / High). High-risk exceptions require Executive approval and may require legal sign-off.
3. Approved exceptions are recorded in the Exceptions Register with mitigation tasks and monitoring requirements.
4. Automated reminders issued 14 days before expiry; renewal requires explicit re-review.

Exception Approval Matrix (summary):
| Risk Rating | Approver | Max Duration | Monitoring Requirements |
|-------------|----------|--------------|-------------------------|
| Low | Security Lead | 180 days | Weekly review by owner |
| Medium | CISO | 90 days | Daily log sampling & alerting |
| High | Executive Security Committee + Legal | 30 days | Continuous monitoring, weekly status reports |

Residual Risk Monitoring:
- Each exception produces a monitoring runbook with telemetry signals and thresholds.
- Security performs monthly reviews of active exceptions and publishes a quarterly summary to leadership.

Appendices

A. Sample IAM policy snippet (service account read-only):
```
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["s3:GetObject"],
      "Resource": ["arn:aws:s3:::redwood-platform-logs/*"]
    }
  ]
}
```

B. Useful CLI and Log Queries:
- Revoke session for user via Okta CLI: okta sessions revoke --user-id <id>
- Example log query (Elasticsearch DSL):
{
  "query": { "bool": { "must": [ { "match": { "event.type": "auth_failure" } }, { "range": { "@timestamp": { "gte": "now-1d/d" } } } ] } }
}

C. Evidence collection checklist (per request):
- [ ] Exported log bundle (UTC timestamps)
- [ ] Snapshot metadata and hash (sha256)
- [ ] SBOM and artifact manifest for implicated release
- [ ] Entitlement report for implicated roles/users
- [ ] Chain-of-custody note and ticket references

D. Escalation & Oncall Roster (summary):
- Security Pager: +1-555-0100 (P1), Mail: security-pager@redwood.example.com
- Compliance: compliance@redwood.example.com
- Legal: legal@redwood.example.com
